why: Array.h constructs and destroys elements in place and names neither <new> nor anything that promises it.
fix: Add #include <new> above <initializer_list>.

why: Same shape as Vector: one argument, no explicit, so an initializer list converts implicitly wherever an Array is expected.
fix: Add explicit; Array.cpp's two Array<int> array({0, 1, ...}) calls already name the object and keep compiling.

why: threads is the container about to receive five threads per round; this reserves capacity on values, the 1000-node payload vector, instead.
fix: Change to threads.reserve(5).

rule: unmapped: unmapped: typo in user-visible text
evidence: "The speicified type is not always lock free on this platfrom.");
why: The static_assert message the engineer sees on a port miss reads speicified and platfrom.
fix: Correct to "The specified type is not always lock free on this platform."

why: Pop hands over ownership of a node the caller must release; discarding the return is a leak, not a no-op.
fix: Mark it [[nodiscard]]; RingQueue's Pop and HashMap's/Map's Insert share the reasoning.

why: priority indexes buckets, a std::array of MaxPriority, with no range test; any MaxPriority below 256 makes a bigger byte an out-of-bounds write.
fix: FatalAssert(priority < MaxPriority, ...) in AcquireBucket, which is where the index is actually formed, and say so on the class page.

why: begin() is the same linear assumption: with head=2 and count=3 in a capacity-4 buffer the real slots are 2,3,0, and this pointer reads 2,3,4.
fix: Fix it together with end(); no test iterates a Deque today, which is why it has never been seen.

why: end() is a linear pointer past head+count, but a Deque stores its elements at WrapIndex(head+i), so once the ring wraps the range walks off the end of the buffer.
fix: Either make Iterator a Deque iterator that carries head and index like HashMap does, or delete begin/end until someone does.

why: COUNT and COUNT2 are UPPER_SNAKE constants; the rule says constants are PascalCase and the rest of the module obeys it (CountBase, NumItems).
fix: Rename to Count and CountRepeat, or better NumNodes and NumPasses, which say what the numbers are.

why: Two different tests register under the identical name, so one result cannot be told from the other in the log the suite exists to produce.
fix: Name the second "Iteration cost"; the first is insertion, this one is repeated traversal.

why: Prefix ++ returns void, so *it++ and every std algorithm that needs Iterator& breaks, while the range-for that works hides it.
fix: Return Iterator& like Map::Iterator and HashMap::Iterator already do.

why: ConstIterator is an alias for the mutable iterator, so a const LinkedList hands out TType& through begin() const and an element can be written through a const view.
fix: Give ConstIterator a const Node* and return const TType&, the way HashMap already does.

why: Move assignment overwrites head and tail without releasing the nodes it already owned, so every element and node of the old list leaks.
fix: Call Clear() first, or delegate to a swap the way Deque and Vector do, so the source releases the destination's old nodes.

why: IsEmpty's own Assert says a null head implies a null tail, which is exactly what Clear leaves broken: head is null, tail is the freed node.
fix: Fixing RemoveNode restores it; until then Clear() followed by any IsEmpty() call trips the assert in Dev.

why: RemoveNode updates only one of head and tail: a node that is both head and tail takes the first branch, so tail keeps the address Unlink is about to free.
fix: Make the two tests independent ifs, and set tail to node->previous in the second; head becomes nullptr when next is, so tail must too.

why: GetNodeOf recovers the node from the payload address, which is only correct while value sits at offset 0, and nothing enforces that.
fix: Add static_assert(offsetof(LinkedListNode<TType>, value) == 0) so the cast cannot silently outlive the layout it depends on.

why: ConstIterator names the mutable iterator, so Find and begin on a const Map return an iterator whose operator* yields Pair&.
fix: Give ConstIterator a const Pair* like HashMap::ConstIterator already does; the alias is one line and the const overloads need no change.

why: Unlike Queue::Pop, this Pop returns the item it removed; dropping it destroys the element and the reader has no clue.
fix: Mark it, and Front, Back and operator[] while the file is open.

why: A single-argument constructor without explicit, so Vector<int> v = {1, 2}; and any TElement converts to a Vector at an argument list.
fix: Add explicit; Vector.cpp's "Vector<int> v = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};" is the one call site that must become brace-initialisation of a named object.

why: Placement new appears 26 times across six of these headers, no file in Engine/Container includes <new>, and a probe that includes only Vector.h still compiles - so the declaration is arriving transitively from libc++ rather than from anything the file declares.
fix: Add #include <new> to Vector.h, Deque.h, Array.h, Map.h, HashMap.h and RingQueue.h, which are the six that use it.

why: Array.h calls allocator.allocate and allocator.deallocate, which DefaultAllocator.h defines; the New/Delete helpers Memory.h names appear nowhere in the file.
fix: Delete the include, or use New<> and Delete<> the way LinkedList.h does, which is the house idiom for an allocator-constructed object.

why: An empty Array holds data == nullptr, and &data[0] on a null pointer is undefined behaviour the optimiser is entitled to use.
fix: Return data and data + length, which are the same pointers without the indexed lvalue.

why: Array::Swap takes an rvalue while Deque, Vector, RingQueue and Map take an lvalue reference, so a.Swap(b) does not compile and Clear() has to construct a temporary to express the same thing.
fix: Take Array& like its four siblings, and let Clear() pass a named empty Array.

evidence: TIndex GetIndex(const Element& element) const noexcept
why: GetIndex answers a question about position and is the only query in the class without [[nodiscard]].
fix: Mark it, and the pair of ToRawArray already are the pattern to follow.

why: The parameter value names the member it initialises, which is the collision the in prefix exists to remove.
fix: Rename the parameter inValue in both constructors.

why: Iterator and ConstIterator are declared and never used: nothing outside this header even names AtomicStackView except MemoryManager's proxyPool.
fix: Delete both aliases, or add the begin/end pair that would make them an iterator.

why: node->next is read from a node a concurrent Pop may already have taken, so a recycler that frees a popped node turns this into a use-after-free.
fix: State the lifetime contract on the class page - nodes must outlive their stay in the view - and consider a tagged pointer or counted head before any owner recycles one.

why: No std::chrono name appears in the file; the timings come from time::TDuration and time::ScopedTime in Core/ScopedTime.h.
fix: Delete the include and let the build gate confirm it.

evidence: TestItem(uint8_t p, bool f = false, uint8_t t = 0)
why: Callable with one argument, so a bare uint8_t converts to a TestItem anywhere one is expected; p, f and t also say nothing.
fix: Add explicit and name the parameters inPriority, inFinished and inTag.

why: The class documentation demands a uint8_t priority and HasFinished() on T, yet nothing checks either, and HasFinished is never called in this header.
fix: Add a requires clause or static_assert for priority, and drop the HasFinished sentence from the contract since Remove takes a predicate instead.

why: The type alias sits between Pop and Remove, in the middle of the public function block, where the twelve-block table wants types first.
fix: Move it to the type block at the top, beside TBucket and TBuckets; layout.py already reports it.

why: 44 asserts in these ten headers fire with no message, so a failed PopFront prints only a file and line, and the reader cannot tell empty-from-uninitialized from emptied.
fix: Give every bounds and empty assert a one-clause message, as RingQueue's "RingQueue is full" already does; the module already carries the pattern.

why: The allocation result is placed-new'd two lines later without a null test; on failure this writes through nullptr.
fix: Validate and log before use, module-wide: Vector.h Reserve, Map.h Grow, HashMap.h Rehash and RingQueue's constructor share the shape.

why: uint8_t is named here and <cstdint> is not among the four standard includes; it reaches the file through DefaultAllocator.h today.
fix: Add #include <cstdint> to the standard block, above <cstddef>.

why: HashMap::Iterator and HashMap::ConstIterator are both inheritable, and both reach callers through Find and begin.
fix: Mark both final.

evidence: explicit Iterator(TMap* map, TIndex index) noexcept
why: Both parameters name the members they initialise, so the initializer list reads map(map), index(index) in two of the module's iterators.
fix: Rename to inMap and inIndex in Iterator and ConstIterator.

evidence: bool Insert(const TKey& key, const TValue& value)
why: The same dropped-result surface as Map: Insert, Remove and operator[] all answer a question the caller can ignore.
fix: Mark them [[nodiscard]] together with Map's, so the two associative containers carry the same contract.

why: The file returns and counts with Index, which Core/Types.h names, without including it; today it arrives through Memory.h.
fix: Add #include "Core/Types.h" to the standard block's project neighbour list.

why: LinkedList::Iterator is the fourth unsealed iterator; 30 of the engine's 61 TestCollection subclasses already carry final, so sealing is the house position, not a new rule.
fix: Mark it final.

why: node(node) again, and this iterator is the one the module's own range-for depends on.
fix: Rename the parameter inNode.

why: FindAndRemove reports whether anything was removed and the caller can drop that on the floor, which is the silent failure the rule exists for.
fix: Mark it [[nodiscard]], and Add/AddLast/AddNext/AddPrevious whose TType& return exists to be used.

why: The three nested iterators a module hands out are the classes a caller is most likely to derive from by accident, and none is sealed.
fix: Mark Iterator and ConstIterator final; the module's own Pair and LinkedListNode already are.

why: The parameter ptr names the member it initialises, which is the collision the in prefix exists to remove; the same shape is in all four nested iterators.
fix: Rename to inPtr here, inNode in LinkedList.h, and inMap and inIndex in HashMap.h.

evidence: bool Insert(const TKey& key, const TValue& value)
why: Insert and Remove return whether the map changed and the result is dropped by the caller as easily as it is honoured.
fix: Mark Insert (all three overloads), Remove and operator[] [[nodiscard]]; Map.cpp already depends on the value inside FatalAssert.

why: InsertSorted default-constructs a TValue and Insert then assigns into it, so TValue must be default-constructible and assignable while nothing says so and a caller learns it from a template error at a distance.
fix: static_assert(std::is_default_constructible_v<TValue> && std::is_assignable_v<TValue&, const TValue&>) on the class, and write the requirement on the class page.

why: A uint8_t block is reinterpret_cast to Pair* with nothing asserting the storage is aligned for Pair, so an over-aligned TValue would be constructed at a misaligned address.
fix: static_assert on alignof(Pair) against the allocator's guarantee, or allocate through DefaultAllocator<Pair> like LinkedList does.

why: Queue.h names no size_t, no nullptr_t and no std::nullptr_t; the header's whole vocabulary is Deque, FatalAssert and std::move.
fix: Delete the include and let the build gate confirm it.

why: Front and Back (both const and not, four functions) and Emplace return the element they exist to hand over, none marked.
fix: Mark them [[nodiscard]]; Size and IsEmpty in the same class already are.

why: The constructor stores the allocation without testing it, so a failed allocate leaves a queue that writes through nullptr on first Push.
fix: Validate and log, in step with Deque::Reserve, Vector::Reserve, Map::Grow, HashMap::Rehash.

why: operator[], Front and Back return the element they were asked for and are not marked, so v[2]; compiles and silently does nothing.
fix: Mark all six [[nodiscard]] like Size and Data already are; Queue.h, RingQueue.h, Deque.h and Array.h have the same gap.

why: A negative newSize takes the shrink branch and destroys data[newSize .. count), which is out of bounds on the low side; nothing rejects it.
fix: FatalAssert(newSize >= 0, "Vector::Resize needs a non-negative size") first, and add the test the suite has none of.

why: Resize is the one growth path that requires TElement to be default-constructible; every other path takes a value, so the requirement arrives only when someone calls Resize.
fix: static_assert(std::is_default_constructible_v<TElement>) beside the class, or take a fill value in Resize's signature.

why: Reserve is the only public mutator in the class without noexcept, and the Rehash it calls is marked; the omission is invisible to a caller choosing between Reserve and Grow.
fix: Mark it noexcept, matching the rest of the file.

why: Remove asserts the address-identity precondition and then calls GetNodeOf, which asserts the identical thing again; two copies of one contract is two places to update.
fix: Keep the assert in GetNodeOf, where the cast lives, and drop the one in Remove.

why: None of the module's ten test fixtures is final, so the one class that can never be a base is declared as if it could.
fix: Add final to all ten; Core's TaskRegistryTest and ResultPacketTest are the model.
